`resolveImageInput` treats any array as raw bytes, so `image: ["data:image/png;base64,..."]` (the shape the codex/nanobanana adapters accept for multi-reference) becomes `Uint8Array.from(["data:..."])` which is `Uint8Array [0]`. That has length 1, passes this check, and Cloudflare gets a 1-byte `input_image_0`, so the caller gets an unconditioned or failed generation instead of the 400 the tests promise for unsupported input.

I'd only take the byte-array branch when every element is an integer 0-255, and otherwise either map string entries to `input_image_0..3` (FLUX.2 accepts up to 4 per the linked changelog) or throw `Invalid reference image`. `body.images` is also ignored here, which is the same silent drop this PR is fixing. A test with `image: [DATA_URL]` would cover it.

Fixed on the current head: `toProviderConnectionResponse()` removes the nested AWS `sessionToken` from create, list, detail, and update responses while keeping it server-side for signing. The Bedrock API regression checks all four responses.

Fixed on the current head. Provider API routes now use `toProviderConnectionResponse()` for create, list, detail, and update, and that helper strips `providerSpecificData.sessionToken` for AWS credential-form providers. The stored token remains available server-side; the API regression asserts it is absent from every response.

Fixed in commit 01ef243: added streamController.handleError(...) on the early-return path, and the message now strips HTML tags and clamps length before reflecting into the client error message to avoid XSS via untrusted upstream text.

Valid catch, fixed in a4e8066. A search scoped away from public web access must not be rerouted through an external provider, that would break the scope the client asked for. prepareWebSearchFallbackBody now returns the body untouched with the fallback disabled whenever any built-in web_search tool carries external_web_access:false, so the whole request goes to the upstream as if this feature did not exist. Covered by a new unit test.

Agreed, and the cleanest way to honor it was to remove the auto-pick entirely (deleted in a4e8066). Before this, an unset webSearchFallbackProvider would scan the provider list and route the search through whichever credentialed provider it found first, which contradicts the "off until configured" claim and could silently send queries through a provider the user never chose for search. Now an empty provider returns a declined search that surfaces to the client as the native error block shape with a message pointing at profile settings. Off-by-default is true end-to-end: no config, no searches, no surprise providers. Test added.
